# Settings file keys

From CMF 1.2.0 a player can choose which map mod wins each feature of the map, and each piece of most features. The easy way is CMF's optional in-game menu add-on, `modCMFInGameMenu`, under Options > Mods > Conjunction Map Framework. Without it, the same choices go into the game's settings file. This page lists every key. [Players' choices](Who-Wins-Each-Feature.md) explains which answer wins when several are set.

## Writing a choice

Close the game first. Open `Documents\The Witcher 3\dx12user.settings` in a text editor and add lines under the `[CMFSettings]` heading (add the heading if it is missing), one choice per line:

```
[CMFSettings]
CMFFile_Icons=modCMFExampleIconPack
CMFFile_Painting_Skellige=Vanilla
```

- **The value** is a map mod's folder name (capital and small letters count the same), `Vanilla` (or `Off`) for the game's own look, or `Automatic` (or `Auto`, `Default`, or nothing) to let the next level decide. Spaces are ignored.
- **One name per value, never a comma.** The game ends a value at its first comma and rewrites the file that way when it exits.
- **A Basic key** (`CMFFile_<Feature>`) chooses for a whole feature. **An Advanced key** (`CMFFile_<Feature>_<Piece>`) chooses for one piece of it and comes before the Basic key.
- **In-game choices come first.** When the menu add-on is installed, its rows and its Mod order decide before any file choice. Without it, file choices decide before the file Mod order.
- **Hidden pins and drawings add together**: every mod's applies. `CMFFile_Hidden` and `CMFFile_Drawings` keep only the named mod's (or none with `Vanilla`), and the three `_Ignore` keys of each leave one mod out each.
- A folder name no installed mod has decides nothing. Values left in the file do nothing once CMF is removed.

`CMFFile_Fallthrough=Vanilla` makes a chosen mod that has nothing for a pin show the game's own look there, instead of the next mod's. `CMFDebug=true` writes the who-wins report to the script log. `CMFLogPins=true` (version 11) writes one line per pin the map shows to the script log, with its type, tag, id and place, so an author can find the name of the one pin they want to change. `CMFMapCheck` (version 11, on when unset) warns once per session when a fully shown world map closes and CMF's map never reported that it loaded, which means another map file loaded in its place; `false` turns the warning off. It does not name the other mod. `CMFProviderOrder1` to `CMFProviderOrder8` hold one folder name each, earliest first.

## The Adapter Check add-on

CMF's optional Adapter Check add-on (API version 11) keeps its own settings: `CMFAdapterCheckEnabled` (on by default) and a hidden `CMFAdapterCheckKnown`, which remembers the set of missing adapters it last warned about. A clean check while it is on clears that memory; while it is off the memory is left alone. From Adapter Check 1.0.1 (with CMF 1.6.0) it logs `adapter check missing mod=.. adapter=..` for each missing adapter, and `adapter check deferred reason=noplayer wait=mapclose` when it waits for the first map close because no player is loaded yet. Once it has shown its box in a game session, an adapter that registers later in that session does not bring the box back.

## Names that kept their old meaning

Choice keys never change once released, so a few names read differently from what they choose today:

- `Size_Lead` and `Size_Spread` (Which pin leads a spread, Stacked pins spread out) and `Labels_Place` (Label place and hiding) belong to Map behaviour, not to Pin size or Pin labels.
- `Colours` in choice keys is the same as `Color` in theme keys and property names.
- `Disabled` in CMF's API (property `5`, `CMFRegisterDisabled`) means a pin a mod greys. In the game's pin types (`...Disabled`) and in `Icons_Completed` it means a completed place.

## Animated pins (API 14)

`[CMFSettings] CMFAnimatedPins` sets how many times a second CMF redraws moving pin pictures. Animations keep their own speed at every setting: a lower rate skips frames rather than slowing them down. `10`, `15` or `30` sets that rate (each divides 30, so redraws land on whole frames); `false` or `0` turns it Off; anything else (missing, empty, `-1`, `true`, `1`, or the retired `20`) is the default, 15. CMF reads it once when the map opens, so changes apply on reopening. Off shows each animation claim's explicit poster, or its first authored frame, with the usual pin looks and no animation clock. It loads only that still picture.

The optional menu's General > Animated pins row stores the option position, as every CMF menu row does: `0` = Off, `1` = 10, `2` = 15, `3` = 30, default `2` (15). A stored answer from `0` to `3` takes precedence over the file switch; a missing, empty or `-1` menu answer falls through to the file. Reset sets the menu answer back to `2` (15). The new row is hidden on older cores.

`[CMFSettings] CMFAnimationDragPause` defaults to On: while the player drags or zooms the map, moving pin pictures hold still and their clocks pause, and they carry on when the map stops. Only `false` or `0` turns it Off. The menu's General > Stop animation during drag row (right under Animated pins) uses Off = `0`, On = `1`, default On, takes precedence when set, and Reset sets it back to On. Both are read once when the map opens.

[CMFSettings] CMFAnimationMemory caps the memory moving pin pictures may use while the map is open, in MB of decoded pictures (4 bytes a pixel): 32, 64 or 128, default 64; any other value is 64. The picture count cap follows it at 64 pictures per MB (4,096 at 64). Pictures past either cap show their still picture, and the log names them (image memory limit). The menu's General > Animation memory row (under Stop animation during drag) stores the option position: 0 = Normal (32 MB), 1 = Large (64 MB, default), 2 = Huge (128 MB); a stored answer takes precedence over the file key, and Reset sets it back to Large. It is read once when the map opens, and the script log shows the chosen ceiling (cacheMb=) with the game's memory figures at open and close.

Animation text belongs only in provider claims. Never write a comma-separated frame list or a `program:v1` descriptor into settings values, choice answers or `CMFFile_` keys: the game truncates settings values at the first comma. Those keys and their provider-name, Vanilla and Automatic answers are unchanged.

The legend uses a type's main still poster, while an explicit legend icon keeps precedence. A native `frame:` poster keeps the existing legend picture. The minimap uses type-level main posters only; it sends only `img://` paths and retains an existing main bitmap or native HUD picture for native-frame posters. It does not play animations or consume under-art claims.
